title: Only Segmented Heavy Tails Can Produce a Light-Tailed Minimum
summary: A random variable $ξ$ has a {\it light-tailed} distribution (for short: is light-tailed) if it possesses a finite exponential moment, $\E \exp (λξ) 0$, and has a {\it heavy-tailed} distribution (is heavy-tailed) if $\E \exp (λξ) = \infty$, for all $λ>0$. In \cite{LSK1}, the authors presented a particular example of a light-tailed random variable that is the minimum of two independent heavy-tailed random variables. In \cite{FKT}, it was shown that any light-tailed random variable with right-unbounded support may be represented as the minimum of two independent heavy-tailed random variables,…
